rules: Glob one prelude: `ruststream_sea_file::file::prelude::*` on a stream file, `ruststream_sea_file::stdio::prelude::*` on a pipeline, and `ruststream_sea_file::prelude::*` only in a service that spans both, where the policies are written `FilePublish` and `StdioPublish`.

Subscribe to a stream file with `#[subscriber(FileStream::new("key"))]`; the bare `#[subscriber("key")]` works on both transports but carries no descriptor, so it describes nothing in the generated AsyncAPI document.

Open a subscription at a position with `start_at(FilePosition::beginning() | end() | sequence(n) | timestamp(millis))`; `FileStream::new(key).replay()` is the separate mode that reads the retained file in one pass and completes at its end.

Reposition a running subscription through the `Ctx<Position>` and `Ctx<SeekHandle>` parameters; both belong to the file transport, and a handler that reads them does not compile against `StdioBroker`.

Name the publish policy `Publish` at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(Marker, Publish)`); neither transport carries per-message settings, so a handler body imports the framework prelude alone and bounds an injected publisher as `Out<impl Publisher, Marker>`.

A `retry_after` copy reaches a stream file under the stream key its subscription reads and needs nothing at the mount site, while a stdio registration must name where the copy goes with `.out_retry(Publish).to("key")` or it refuses to start.

Cap circulating retries with `.max_attempts(n)` and `.dead_letter("key")` right after `include`; the count is the framework's retry-count header, because neither transport counts its own redeliveries.

Take batches with a `&[T]` handler and `.batch(n)` at the mount site; both clients read one entry at a time, so a batch is assembled on the client and a partial one goes out 10 ms after its first delivery.

Do not rely on acknowledgement: `ack` and `nack` report `AckError::Unsupported` on both transports, so a service resumes by storing a `FilePosition` and reopening with `start_at(..)`, or by replaying the file.

Unit-test handlers with `ruststream::testing::TestApp` against `FileTestBroker` or `StdioTestBroker` behind the `testing` feature, keeping the descriptor and the policy the service ships with; there is no harness-only policy to swap in.
